_what: Standing director crossing rulings, read BY tools/batch_test/soak/wave_fence.py itself on every run (RULING 11, GH #729). A ruling that lives only in a report, a charter, or three flags the operator has to retype is a ruling whose default state is silence -- that is what cost W64.
_who_writes_this: The director, in the same work unit as the ruling. Nobody else. The batch desk READS it (by running the gate); it does not add rows.
_constraints: Every record goes through wave_fence.build_crossing(), so RULING 10's four constraints hold verbatim: the ceiling cannot reach the $90 brake or the owner's $100 approval line (refused, exit 2, never clamped); `expiry` is mandatory and checked at run time; `ref` is mandatory and printed verbatim; the gate announces the ruling on every run it touches, including the CLEAR one.
_expiry_semantics: An expired record here is NOT an error -- it is a record reaching its designed end of life. The gate keeps running, at the DERIVED fence, and says out loud that the ruling expired. (An expired ruling asserted via --director-crossing IS exit 2: there the operator claimed this round that it was live.) Retire expired records when convenient; leaving one costs a printed line, not a gate.
_two_live_at_once: Refused, exit 2. Which ceiling binds would otherwise be a bookkeeping accident. Superseding a ruling means removing the old row in the same edit.
_a_crossing_can_change_sign: RULING 15 (GH #754, 2026-09-11). A crossing is applied as `min(ruling, brake)`, and that min has no floor -- so the SAME record raises the ceiling while the derived fence sits below it and LOWERS the ceiling the moment the derived fence rises above it. Nothing about the record changes; the tree moves under it. A crossing ruling therefore has to be re-read whenever MTD crosses a budget alert, because that is exactly when the derived fence jumps and the sign can flip. Measured, not asserted: see `_retired[0]`.

_retired.note: RULING 10. September remaining operative ceiling $85.00. The $90 brake and the owner's $100 approval line are untouched; $5 is deliberately left between $85 and the brake. Buys roughly $7 of headroom over the derived $80 fence, about 6 spot waves. Reason: the $80 fence is an ACCOUNT number and ~48% of September MTD is a co-tenant workload with its own budget.
_retired.retirement_reason: ITS SIGN FLIPPED, AND ITS OWN NOTE SAYS WHEN. The note prices the record against a DERIVED FENCE OF $80. On 2026-09-11 MTD reached $80.413, i.e. the $80 ACTUAL alert was crossed, so the lowest uncrossed alert -- the derived fence -- became $100.00 and min(fence, brake) became the $90.00 brake. From that instant `min(ruling=85, brake=90)` no longer bought $5; it SOLD $5. Offline replay of the batch desk's own 18:15Z figures (--actual 80.413 --limit 100 --thresholds 50,80,100 --pending 3.45 --no-accrual-check): the gate-(iv)-mandated on-demand wave (--planned 2.15) is exit 3 with the record in force (`Headroom was $1.137, this wave needs $2.150`) and exit 0 with --no-crossing-file (`operative ceiling $90.00`, `headroom $3.987 after this wave`). The whole of GH #754's scissors was this record. Retiring it authorises NO new money: the ceiling simply returns to the $90 brake the tool derives on its own.
